title: A Unified Rational-Function Approximation for Square-Well, Square-Shoulder, and Nonadditive Hard-Sphere Mixtures
authors: Andrés Santos, Santos B. Yuste, Ana M. Montero, Mariano López de Haro
abstract: We develop a rational-function approximation for the structural properties of multicomponent fluids with narrow square-well and square-shoulder interactions, together with weakly nonadditive hard-sphere mixtures. The theory is obtained by reformulating the analytical Percus--Yevick solution for additive sticky hard-sphere mixtures so as to account for finite interaction widths, leading to a unified semianalytical framework for these classes of fluids. The approximation satisfies the exact low-density limit and preserves the continuity of the cavity functions; a simple local correction restores the continuity of their first derivatives. Comparison with Monte Carlo simulations for binary mixtures shows that the theory accurately describes both the radial distribution functions and their Fourier transforms for narrow wells and shoulders and for weak nonadditivity. The proposed formulation extends previous sticky-hard-sphere-based approaches while retaining their analytical simplicity.
summary: This paper introduces a unified Rational-Function Approximation (RFA) to calculate the structural properties of complex fluids featuring square-well, square-shoulder, and nonadditive hard-sphere interactions. By reformulating the Percus-Yevick theory, the authors provide a semi-analytical framework that accurately predicts radial distribution functions across various regimes. This work advances the theoretical understanding of liquid structure in systems with complex, short-range potentials.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a unified rational-function approximation (RFA) for the structural properties of multicomponent fluids interacting via square-well, square-shoulder, and weakly nonadditive hard-sphere potentials.
main_result: The proposed RFA provides an accurate, semi-analytical framework that successfully models the radial distribution functions and their Fourier transforms for these complex fluid mixtures, matching Monte Carlo simulations.
method: The theory reformulates the analytical Percus-Yevick solution for sticky hard-sphere mixtures, extending it to incorporate finite interaction widths and nonadditivity through a rational-function approximation.
model_or_system: The study focuses on multicomponent fluids modeled using hard-core interactions augmented by square-well (SW), square-shoulder (SS), and weakly nonadditive hard-sphere (NAHS) potentials. It analyzes binary and ternary mixtures.
key_observables: Radial distribution functions ($g_{ij}(r)$) and their Fourier transforms ($h_{ij}(q)$).
important_parameters: Interaction parameters ($\epsilon_{ij}, \Delta_{ij}$), density ($ho$), and the narrow-shell limit ($\Delta_{ij} \ll \sigma_{ij}$).
main_assumptions: The approximation relies on reformulating the PY solution and requires imposing a closure assumption to determine the necessary coefficients.
figures_summary: The figures compare the RFA results against Monte Carlo simulations and the PY-SHS prediction for various binary (SW, SS, NAHS) and ternary systems, showing agreement across different densities and interaction strengths.
paper_structure: The paper develops the RFA by building upon the PY-SHS solution, deriving the approximation through formal parameterization, and validating the results by comparing the predicted structural functions against extensive Monte Carlo simulation data across multiple interaction regimes.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluids, the development of highly accurate, analytically tractable approximations for complex many-body systems (like the RFA) is a valuable theoretical tool applicable to modeling interacting quantum systems where exact solutions are intractable.
